text:
incident-bot: Paging: alice (oncall) — SEV2 alert: embed-service error rate spike in us-west-2 (>25% 5m). Alert: https://alerts.redwood.example/ALERT-4312

alice (oncall): acked, jumping in. Seeing 502 spikes on the embedding endpoint. Putting brief notes here so handoff is clear.

ben (sre): on it. quick check — is this client-side retry flood or backend OOMs? can you paste head of logs from one failing host?

alice (oncall): tail from gw-embed-03: 
```
2026-03-14T13:04:12Z ERROR handler.go:213 upstream: upstream error: kvcache miss + timeout
2026-03-14T13:04:12Z ERROR runtime.go:89 oom: attempted alloc 1.4GB, available 0.8GB
```

ben (sre): ok looks like memory pressure on a subset of pods causing 502s. probable cascade due to kvcache growth. mitigation plan: 1) scale up pool to drain pressure, 2) temporarily disable prefix caching for embeds, 3) route traffic to warm instances.

alice (oncall): scaling now — increasing embed-pool to 12 replicas (was 6). devops-bot, please confirm autoscaler applied.

devops-bot: Autoscaling event triggered for service embed-service: desired=12 current=6. New nodes provisioning in us-west-2. Status: 4/6 ready, expected 12 in ~90s.

dave (support): Heads up — Support is seeing multiple customers with timeouts and 429 retries. Customer-facing summary? Any ETA for improvement?

alice (oncall): tell Support: we're seeing internal memory pressure causing upstream 502s on embeddings in us-west-2. We're scaling and disabling a cache knob; ETA 3-5 mins for measurable improvement. Will update.

carol (product): tagging customer-impact tracker: would love customer list if available. Also we should check if any enterprise tenants were affected (dedicated vs hosted).

erin (ml): quick note — we rolled a kvcache growth change last week for longer prefix retention; might be related. If we disable retention it'll free memory. How do we toggle?

ben (sre): toggle is config flag `kvcache.prefix_retention_ms`. Setting to 30000 from 300000 will reduce retention. Alice, can you apply as emergency config?

alice (oncall): applying change via config rollout to embed-config -> setting prefix_retention_ms=30000. Rolling one shard at a time with 30s pause. Command: 
```bash
redwoodctl rollout set-config embed-config --set kvcache.prefix_retention_ms=30000 --rolling --pause 30s
```

devops-bot: Rollout started for embed-config. 1/4 shards updated. No deploy yet.

ben (sre): also advise to warm instances before moving production traffic. frank, can you spin up two warm boxes and attach them to pool?

frank (eng): on it — launching warm instances now, will attach to pool via `attach-warm --service=embed-service --count=2`.

(devops-bot): Warm instances attached. Healthchecks passing.

alice (oncall): seeing error rate drop to ~6% now. 502s down from 25%. Scaling + config change helped. Keeping watch.

dave (support): passing update to impacted customers. appreciate the quick turnaround.

carol (product): thanks team. Next steps: full postmortem, RCA, and follow-ups. Can we schedule a postmortem review in sync with a brown-bag knowledge share next week? Prefer Wed 10am PT.

erin (ml): I can present the kvcache retention change and rationale in the brown-bag. Suggest also covering cache telemetry improvements.

ben (sre): action items (assigning here):
- ALICE: write incident timeline and initial mitigations in the postmortem doc (due EOD tomorrow)
- BEN: add memory / kvcache retention metrics to the runtime dashboards and set an alert on kvcache size (due 2 business days)
- FRANK: add a warm instance playbook for embed-service in runbook repo (due 3 business days)
- ERIN: prepare brown-bag slides and a couple short demos of retention knobs (due 5 business days)
- DAVE: compile list of customers impacted and paste into postmortem (due EOD tomorrow)

alice (oncall): I’ll start the postmortem doc, link: https://docs.redwood.example/postmortems/pm-4312. I’ll add notes & timeline. Feel free to add comments.

carol (product): For severity/perf classification: propose Sev2 -> Postmortem + Exec summary + Customer follow-up. Agree?

ben (sre): agree. We'll run retrospective in the postmortem doc. Also propose immediate short-term guardrail: set kvcache size soft-limit and alert.

frank (eng): question — do we want automatic fallback to smaller quantized model variant when memory > threshold? Could reduce memory pressure but might affect quality. Worth discussing in postmortem.

erin (ml): I can evaluate auto-fallback impact on output quality and latency. Add as follow-up action for Optimize team.

alice (oncall): thanks all. Handoff to next oncall (ben taking over monitoring). I’m tagging this thread as the source for the postmortem.

ben (sre): I’ll monitor next 2 hours, will escalate if regression. Adding a short retro + brown-bag invite: Wed 2026-03-18 10:00 PT — calendar invite to follow. :calendar: :white_check_mark:

carol (product): thanks team — great mitigation. We'll use the postmortem to capture prevention patterns and runbook updates. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident ALARM cleared at 2026-03-14T13:12:10Z. Duration: ~8m. Severity: SEV2. Postmortem link: https://docs.redwood.example/postmortems/pm-4312

alice (oncall): closing thread, moving to postmortem channel and scheduling brown-bag. Good job everyone. :rocket:
